boundaries: Evaluation is not Validation unless its profile is a validation profile.
Evaluation output is not an authority decision.
claim_ceiling: This candidate defines Evaluation semantics only. It neither performs an evaluation nor determines conformance or admission.

scope.applicability: The application of one exact evaluation profile to one exact subject and input state, collecting every declared check outcome and causal dependency.
exclusions: A claim that the subject conforms.
A human admission or acceptance decision.
An effectful execution not explicitly included in the profile.

examples: An Artifact Type evaluation records schema and semantic-reference checks.
A blocked source dependency makes dependent checks NOT_EVALUABLE, not absent or PASS.
domain_context.explanation: CML-07 uses collect-all evaluations to expose all schema, reference, projection, and dependency outcomes before the one configured owner boundary.

plain_language.explanation: An Evaluation runs a declared set of checks against exact inputs and records every result, including the checks that could not yet be evaluated.

boundary_conditions: The profile, subject, and inputs are exact and current.
Dependent checks are recorded as NOT_EVALUABLE rather than omitted.
An evaluation result remains inside the profile's coverage.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: evaluate(P@digest, S@digest, I@digest) -> O = {(check_id, PASS|FAIL|NOT_EVALUABLE, evidence_refs, blockers)}; O =/=> admitted(S).
scientific_formal.normative_statement: An Evaluation applies a version-exact profile P to a version-exact subject S and input state I, yielding a complete outcome set O with causal blockers preserved. Evaluation is an evidence-producing process; its outcomes do not exceed P's declared coverage or create authority.

notation.meaning: The collect-all set of declared check outcomes.

testable_conditions: Every declared check has an outcome.
Every NOT_EVALUABLE outcome names its causal blocker.
The evaluation identifies exact profile and subject digests.
